Last summer I went to Beijing with my German boss, who was giving a talk, and I was in charge of interpreting. I assumed I’d need to interpret live, so I did some preparation in advance. Even so, a few times during the talk I had no idea how to translate something:

1. Names. Most well-known scientists have Chinese versions of their names, but I first came across them in English;

2. Technical terms I had missed while preparing the day before;

3. Other expressions that have no suitable Chinese equivalent.

So when talking with other Chinese people abroad, we just say all of these in English. Of course, if you throw technical terms at Chinese people outside your field, they probably won’t understand them in Chinese or in English...
